chunks: And in the narration of al-‘Abbās ibn Hilāl, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, that he said:
“Whoever gives the adhan and the iqamah, two rows of angels pray behind him; and if he gives the iqamah without an adhan, one prays on his right and one on his left.”
Then he said: “Take advantage of the two rows.”

key_terms.أَذَّنَ: gave the adhan, the call announcing the prayer
key_terms.أَقَامَ: gave the iqamah, the call establishing the start of prayer
key_terms.اغْتَنِمِ: seize the opportunity or benefit from it
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةِ: the angels who pray behind or beside the worshipper
key_terms.صَفَّانِ: two rows, referring here to rows of angels

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting both the adhan and iqamah before prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith encourages performing both the adhan and the iqamah before salat by describing the spiritual reward attached to them. It teaches that the one who does so is accompanied by two rows of angels, and even performing only the iqamah still brings angelic presence, making this a strong exhortation toward observing the full prayer call.
